newsitem.title: CONGO: Mediators announce weekend Congo peace talks plan.
newsitem.headline: Mediators announce weekend Congo peace talks plan.

text.p: Mediators trying to end a bloody standoff in the former French colony of Congo said on Friday that President Pascal Lissouba and his predecessor and rival Denis Sassou Nguesso would meet in Gabon on Sunday.

A spokesman for Lissouba said that a mediation committee led by Brazzaville mayor Bernard Kolelas had proposed the meeting to end over a week of clashes between supporters of the two men but could not confirm that Lissouba would be going.
"The two protagonists and the mediation committee chairman are to meet in Libreville with (Gabon's) President (Omar) Bongo," Hellot Mampouya, a spokesman for Kolelas, told reporters.

"The meeting will probably take place on Sunday because tomorrow representatives of Lissouba and Sassou will meet with the mediating committee which will discuss the points which will be on the agenda at the negotiations," he said.
Neither Sassou Nguesso nor a spokesman was immediately available for comment.
Fighting broke out on June 5 after soldiers surrounded Sassou Nguesso's home as part of a crackdown on private militias and illegal possession of arms in the runup to July 27 elections.
